Ltd.]] (20%) | chairman = [[Sanjiv Goenka]] | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Panagiotis Dilberis|Panagiotis Dilmperis]] | league = {{Indian football updater|MBSG}} | season = {{Indian football updater|MBSG2}} | position = {{Indian football updater|MBSG3}} | current = 2026–27 Mohun Bagan Super Giant season | pattern_la1 = _mbsg2023h | pattern_b1 = _mbsg2023h | pattern_ra1 = _mbsg2024h | pattern_sh1 = | pattern_so1 = _mbsg2023h | leftarm1 = | body1 = | rightarm1 = | shorts1 = 7A1024 | socks1 = | pattern_la2 = _mbsg2023a | pattern_b2 = _mbsg2023a | pattern_ra2 = _mbsg2023a | pattern_sh2 = | pattern_so2 = _mbsg2023a | leftarm2 = | body2 = | rightarm2 = | shorts2 = | kit_alt3 = | pattern_la3 = | pattern_b3 = | pattern_ra3 = | pattern_sh3 = | pattern_so3 = | leftarm3 = | body3 = | rightarm3 = | shorts3 = | socks3 = | website = {{URL|https://mohunbaganclub.com}} }} '''[[Mohun Bagan Super Giant]]''', commonly referred to as '''Mohun Bagan''' ({{ipa|bn|moɦɔn baɡan|lang}}), is an Indian professional [[association football|football]] club based in [[Kolkata]], [[West Bengal]]. Founded in 1889, it is one of the oldest football clubs in [[Asia]]. The club competes in the [[Indian Super League]], the top tier of the [[Indian football league system]]. They are the [[List of Indian football champions|most successful club in India]] and one of the most successful in [[Asia]], winning a record cumulative number of [[list of Mohun Bagan Super Giant records and statistics|265 trophies]]. They have won more than 5,000 matches in their football history, which is the highest by an Asian club. The club's first notable victory came against the [[East Yorkshire Regiment]] in the 1911 [[IFA Shield]] final, when its players played barefooted. This victory made Mohun Bagan the first all-Indian club to win championship over a British club, and was a major moment during India's push for [[Indian independence movement|independence]].{{cite web|url=https://thesefootballtimes.co/2015/03/22/mohun-bagan-and-the-fight-for-indian-independence/|title=MOHUN BAGAN AND THE FIGHT FOR INDIAN INDEPENDENCE|date=22 March 2015 |access-date=7 November 2023|archive-date=7 November 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231107041408/https://thesefootballtimes.co/2015/03/22/mohun-bagan-and-the-fight-for-indian-independence/|url-status=live}} The club was founded as Mohun Bagan Sporting Club in 1889, which was later changed to Mohun Bagan Athletic Club and often shortened to just Mohun Bagan. From 1998 to 2015, the club took on the name McDowell Mohun Bagan due to sponsorship reasons. In 2017, Mohun Bagan Football Club (India) Pvt Ltd was created as the legal footballing entity of Mohun Bagan Athletic Club. On 16 January 2020, it was announced that the [[RPSG Group]] (KGSPL), the owners of [[ATK (football club)|ATK FC]], along with former cricketer Sourav Ganguly and businessmen Utsav Parekh, acquired an 80% stake in Mohun Bagan Football Club (India) Pvt Ltd. [[ATK (football club)|ATK FC]] was officially disbanded on 1 July 2020, and Mohun Bagan entered the [[Indian Super League]] in the [[2020–21 Indian Super League|2020-21 season]] with the name ATK Mohun Bagan FC. In 2023, after severe protests from the Mohun Bagan supporters all around, KGSPL removed the term ATK and changed the name to Mohun Bagan Super Giant. Mohun Bagan have won a record [[List of Indian football champions|7 Indian League]] titles {{Emdash}} the [[National Football League (India)|National Football League]] 3 times, the [[I-League]] 2 times and the [[Indian Super League#Regular season|Indian Super League Shield]] 2 times. They are the most successful Indian club in the history of the [[Federation Cup (India)|Federation Cup]], having won the championship a record 14 times.{{cite web |date=10 January 2015 |title=From the The first trophy won by Mohun Bagan was the [[Cooch Behar Cup]] in 1904, which they have won a record 18 times. In the [[2024–25 Indian Super League]], Mohun Bagan became the first club to successfully defend the [[Indian Super League|League Shield]] and 7th Indian League title. Mohun Bagan achieved the league and cup double for the first time. In the same season, Mohun Bagan became the 1st ISL club to cross the '''50''' seasonal points. The club annually contests in Asia's oldest and biggest rivalry, the [[Kolkata Derby]] against its long-time local rival [[East Bengal FC|East Bengal]],{{cite web |last=Choudhury |first=Angikaar |date=8 September 2015 |title=The East Bengal-Mohun Bagan Derby: The Rivalry That Divides Kolkata |url=https://scroll.in/field/754003/the-east-bengal-mohun-bagan-derby-the-rivalry-that-divides-kolkata |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624200207/https://scroll.in/field/754003/the-east-bengal-mohun-bagan-derby-the-rivalry-that-divides-kolkata |archive-date=24 June 2021 |access-date=17 June 2021 |website=[[Scroll.in|Scroll]]}} with the first derby match being played on 8 August 1921.{{cite web |last=Sharma |first=Amitabha Das |date=1 April 2016 |title=The Kolkata Derby: They Met as Early as 1921! |url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/football/the-kolkata-derby-they-met-as-early-as-in-1921/article17221788.ece |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230416103239/https://sportstar.thehindu.com/football/the-kolkata-derby-they-met-as-early-as-in-1921/article17221788.ece |archive-date=16 April 2023 |access-date=19 May 2023 |website=[[Sportstar]]}} Mohun Bagan was one of the founding members of National Football League in 1996, and has never been relegated from the top-tier league of the country. On 29 July 2019, during its 130th year, the club was inducted into the "[[Club of Pioneers]]", a network of the oldest existing football clubs around the world.{{Cite web|date=17 May 2019|title=How will Mohun Bagan benefit from their inclusion in the Club of Pioneers?|url=https://khelnow.com/football/i-league-2019-20-mohun-bagan-club-of-pioneers-benefits/|access-date=2 January 2021|website=Khel Now|language=en-US|archive-date=29 October 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211029110707/https://khelnow.com/football/i-league-2019-20-mohun-bagan-club-of-pioneers-benefits|url-status=live}}{{TOC limit|2}} == History == {{Main|History of Mohun Bagan Super Giant}} === Early years (1889–99) === [[Mohun Bagan AC|Mohun Bagan]] was established on 15 August 1889, with [[Bhupendra Nath Bose]] becoming the first president of the newly founded club and Jyotindra Nath Bose the first secretary of it. Mohun Bagan played their first match in 1889 against the team of [[Eden Hindu Hostel]] students and lost 1–0.{{cite web |last1=Mukherjee |first1=Anita |date=10 July 2021 |title=MOHUN BAGAN VILLA – GONE, BUT NOT FORGOTTEN |url=https://breathingroots.co.in/2020/10/10/mohun-bagan-villa-gone-but-not-forgotten/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221003050014/https://breathingroots.co.in/2020/10/10/mohun-bagan-villa-gone-but-not-forgotten/ |archive-date=3 October 2022 |access-date=5 May 2022 |website=Breathing Roots}}{{cite web |title=The Beginning – 1889 to 1909 |url=http://www.mohunbaganclub.com/history/history-1889-1909/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20150505103851/http://www.mohunbaganclub.com/history/history-1889-1909/ |archive-date=5 May 2015 |access-date=5 May 2022 |website=Mohun Bagan Club}} The initial players to play for the club were Girin Basu, Pramatha Nath Chattopadhyay, Sachin Bandhyopadhyay, Ram Goswami, Sarat Mitra, Hem Nath Sen, Nalin Basu, Upen Ghosh, Manindra Nath Basu, Manomoham Pandey, Probhas Mitra, and the captain Manilal Sen.{{cite web |title=The Beginning – 1889 to 1909 |url=http://www.mohunbaganclub.com/history/history-1889-1909/ |website=Mohun Bagan Club |access-date=5 May 2022 |archive-date=5 May 2015 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20150505103851/http://www.mohunbaganclub.com/history/history-1889-1909/ |url-status=live }} The first tournament that the club participated in was the 1893 [[Cooch Behar Cup|Coochbehar Cup]], where the team suffered to perform against the [[British Indian Army]] teams and the clubs like [[Aryan FC|Aryan]], National, Town Club, Kumurtuli, Fort William's Arsenal and the famed Sovabazar, which was founded by the ''Father of Indian football'' [[Nagendra Prasad Sarbadhikari]] himself. === Colonial era === The early exits from major tournaments suffered in the 1900s evoked ridicule from its local rivals, including Sovabazar. Soon after the appointment of [[Subedar-major]] Sailen Basu as the secretary, the club adopted European playing methods and players underwent rigorous physical training and followed austere fitness regime similar to that in the army. The club also began recruiting players from other clubs, especially from National, where footballers played in boots rather than barefoot. [[The Reverend|Rev.]] [[Sudhir Kumar Chatterjee|Sudhir Chatterjee]] was one of the notable recruitments from National, who was also the only player in the club to play in boots at that time. As a result, the club achieved its first success by winning the 1904 Coochbehar Cup.{{cite web |last1=Sengupta |first1=Somnath |date=2 May 2010 |title=History Of Mohun Bagan (Part 1): The Success That Changed Indian Football |url=http://www.thehardtackle.com/2010/history-of-mohun-bagan-chapter-1-the-origin-and-the-success-that-changed-indian-football/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211025110131/http://www.thehardtackle.com/2010/history-of-mohun-bagan-chapter-1-the-origin-and-the-success-that-changed-indian-football/ |archive-date=25 October 2021 |access-date=5 May 2022 |website=The Hard Tackle}} The following year Mohun Bagan won the Coochbehar Cup once again and reached the Gladstone Cup final, held in [[Hugli-Chuchura|Chinsurah]], where they defeated the reigning [[IFA Shield]] champions [[Dalhousie AC|Dalhousie]] 6–1, with [[Shibdas Bhaduri]] scoring four goals.{{cite web |last=Saha |first=Nirmal Kumar |date=29 July 2020 |title=বিপ্র-কুটিরের 'পঞ্চম পাণ্ডব' শিবদাস |trans-title='Fifth Pandava' Shibdas of Bipra-Kutir |url=https://thecalcuttamirror.com/daily-news/kolkata/2245/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221021164919/https://thecalcuttamirror.com/daily-news/kolkata/2245/ |archive-date=21 October 2022 |access-date=20 October 2022 |website=thecalcuttamirror.com |publisher=The Calcutta Mirror |language=bn |agency= |location=Kolkata}} [[Maharaja]] Rajendra Bhup Bahadur of [[Cooch Behar State|Coochbehar]], impressed by the team, would become a chief patron of the club. In 1906, Mohun Bagan also won the Minto Fort Tournament by defeating one of the major [[England|English]] clubs in India, [[Calcutta Cricket and Football Club|Calcutta]]. But they were disqualified for the 1906 IFA Shield because P.K. Biswas, who had played for both National and Mohun Bagan in the same year, which was considered illegal by the [[Indian Football Association]], the then ''de facto'' governing body of Indian football. Apart from team building, Subedar-major Basu had a remarkable contribution in arranging a new club tent and ground after the demolition of Mohun Bagan Villa in 1891. The club did not have a permanent club tent, but the number of club members increased due to minimal membership fees of at most 8 [[Anna (monetary subunit)|annas]]. During this period a major meeting was held among the club officials including Jyotindra Nath Basu, Subedar-major Sailen Basu, Dwijendra Nath Basu, [[Bhupendra Nath Mitra|Sir Bhupendra Nath Mitra]] and Dr. Girish Ghosh and soon the club tent within Mohun Bagan's premises in [[Maidan (Kolkata)|Maidan]] was constructed. Mohun Bagan won the Trades Cup four consecutive times between 1906 and 1909, which was the second most prestigious tournament in India after IFA Shield. Mohun Bagan won Coochbehar Cup in 1907 and 1908, and then both the Laxmibilas Cup and the Gladstone Cup in 1909 and 1910. In 1909 and 1910, among only a few other native clubs, the team had the honor to play in the IFA Shield for its consistent performances over the recent years. However, they would struggle to match the [[regiment]]al teams of [[British Army|British]] and [[British Indian Army|British Indian]] armies in the first two years of participation. === The historic year of 1911 === [[File:Mohun_Bagan_1911_IFA_shield_winning_team.jpg|left|thumb|A colourized image of the [[IFA Shield]] winning team of 1911]] In 1911, Mohun Bagan formed a dominant side for the IFA Shield,{{Cite web |last=Sengupta |first=Somnath |date=29 July 2011 |title=Tactical Evolution Of Indian Football (Part One): Profiling Three Great 2–3–5 Teams |url=https://thehardtackle.com/2011/tactical-evolution-of-indian-football-part-one-profiling-three-great-2-3-5-teams/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211009112727/https://thehardtackle.com/2011/tactical-evolution-of-indian-football-part-one-profiling-three-great-2-3-5-teams/ |archive-date=9 October 2021 |access-date=16 March 2021 |website=thehardtackle.com |publisher=The Hard Tackle |language=en-US |location=Kolkata}} which included [[Hiralal Mukherjee]], Bhuti Sukul, Rev. Sudhir Chatterjee, Monmohun Mukherjee, Rajen Sengupta, Nil Madhav Bhattacharya, Kanu Roy, Habul Sarkar, Abhilash Ghosh, Bijoydas Bhaduri and captained by [[Shibdas Bhaduri]].{{cite web |title=Creation of History – 1910 to 1919 |url=http://www.mohunbaganclub.com/history/632-2/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220505210601/http://www.mohunbaganclub.com/history/632-2/ |archive-date=5 May 2022 |access-date=5 May 2022 |website=Mohun Bagan Club}}{{cite web |last1=Bhattacharya |first1=Nilesh |date=22 August 2023 |title=Mad about football |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/kolkata/mad-about-football/articleshow/102933485.cms |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230823180930/https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/kolkata/mad-about-football/articleshow/102933485.cms |archive-date=23 August 2023 |access-date=22 February 2024 |website=timesofindia.indiatimes.com |publisher=[[The Times of India]] |agency=TNN |location=Kolkata}} They battled out against the professionally equipped teams of [[St. Xavier's College, Kolkata|St. Xavier's College]], Calcutta Rangers Club, [[Rifle Brigade (The Prince Consort's Own)|Rifle Brigade]] and [[Middlesex Regiment]] to reach the IFA Shield final without conceding a goal. The enthusiasm for the [[1911 IFA Shield final|final]], held on 29 July 1911, was such that people came from other [[district]]s of [[Bengal Presidency|Bengal]] as well as from neighboring provinces of [[Bihar and Orissa Province|Bihar]] and [[Eastern Bengal and Assam Province|Assam]]. The [[East Indian Railway Company]] ran a special train and additional steamer services were pressed into service to ferry spectators to [[Kolkata|Calcutta]] from the ''mofussil'' areas. Tickets for the match, originally priced at {{Indian Rupee|1}} and {{Indian Rupee|2}}, were sold at {{Indian Rupee|15}} due to its immense demand in the region. After trailing by a goal from [[Sergeant|Sgt.]] Jackson of [[East Yorkshire Regiment]] team within the first 15 minutes of the 50 minute-match, Shibdas Bhaduri soon scored an equalizer in the first half and then set up Abhilash Ghosh to score the winner with just two minutes remaining.{{cite web |title=List of IFA Shield Finals |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesi/india-ifahist.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121031142319/http://rsssf.com/tablesi/india-ifahist.html |archive-date=31 October 2012 |access-date=20 November 2012 |publisher=Rec.Sport.Soccer Statistics Foundation}} The club became the first native team to lift the IFA Shield, that too in front of an estimated crowd of 80,000, although the referee, H.G. Pooler, estimated approximately 20,000 to be the number.{{cite web |last1=Basu |first1=Jaydeep |date=29 July 2020 |title=A victory for India? Why Mohun Bagan's historic 1911 IFA Shield win was purely about football |url=https://scroll.in/field/968849/why-mohun-bagans-historic-1911-ifa-shield-win-should-be-judged-purely-from-a-football-perspective#:~:text=Manchester%20Guardian%20reported%20there%20were,%2C%20however%2C%20viewed%20it%20differently. |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220505210600/https://scroll.in/field/968849/why-mohun-bagans-historic-1911-ifa-shield-win-should-be-judged-purely-from-a-football-perspective#:~:text=Manchester%20Guardian%20reported%20there%20were,%2C%20however%2C%20viewed%20it%20differently. |archive-date=5 May 2022 |access-date=5 May 2022 |website=Scroll}} Mohun Bagan supporters and the public at large went berserk, even supporters of [[Muslims|Muslim]] representative clubs like Moslem and [[Mohammedan SC (Kolkata)|Mohammedan]] went to the streets to celebrate and the Muslims from [[Dharmatala]] joined the victory procession of [[Hindus]] near the [[Thanthania Kalibari]].{{cite web |last1=Majumdar |first1=Boria |date=22 July 2010 |title=The Victory |url=https://openthemagazine.com/sports/the-victory/ |access-date=5 May 2022 |publisher=Open}}{{cite web |date=16 November 2014 |title=Mohammedan Sporting: A football club with legacy that needs understanding |url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/football/mohammedan-sporting-football-club-legacy-needs-understanding |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220505210608/https://www.sportskeeda.com/football/mohammedan-sporting-football-club-legacy-needs-understanding |archive-date=5 May 2022 |access-date=5 May 2022 |website=Sportskeeda}} Based on a popular legend, after the match ended, a [[Brahmin]], pointing to the [[Union Jack]] fluttering atop [[Fort William, Kolkata|Fort William]], asked Rev. Chatterjee, "When will that come down?" and was predicted that the flag would come down only when Mohun Bagan wins the shield next time, which coincidentally came true. === Nation-wide exposure of the club (1912–30) === After a comparatively disappointing year in 1912, Shibdas Bhaduri handed the captaincy to Habul Sarkar the following year, but they failed to win any trophy that year. The same year [[Gostha Pal]] joined the club as a [[Defender (association football)|defender]] at the young age of 16 and soon became known as the ''"Chinese Wall"'' for his defensive prowess.{{Cite web |date=20 August 2020 |title=A Legend Without Shoes, This 'Chinese Wall' Was Once India's Favourite Footballer |url=https://www.thebetterindia.com/236100/gostha-pal-paul-kolkata-football-legend-birth-anniversary-first-padma-shri-award-postage-stamp-mohun-bagan-club-ser106/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220505213849/https://www.thebetterindia.com/236100/gostha-pal-paul-kolkata-football-legend-birth-anniversary-first-padma-shri-award-postage-stamp-mohun-bagan-club-ser106/ |archive-date=5 May 2022 |access-date=5 May 2022 |website=The Better India |language=en}} In 1914, Mohun Bagan for the first time played in [[Calcutta Football League|CFL]] 2nd Division and finished third, but got promoted after a team from the 1st Division withdrew. Mohun Bagan played their first match on 15 May 1915 against Calcutta, which was drawn.{{Cite web |last=Andrew Flint |date=11 November 2015 |title=A Tale of One City: Kolkata |url=https://thesefootballtimes.co/2015/11/11/a-tale-of-one-city-kolkata/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210709183002/https://thesefootballtimes.co/2015/11/11/a-tale-of-one-city-kolkata/ |archive-date=9 July 2021 |access-date=16 March 2021 |website=These Football Times |language=en-GB}} Meanwhile, Subedar-major Basu had to leave for his commitments in the military service for the [[World War I]] and Dwijendra Nath Basu, nephew of Bhupendra Nath Basu and brother of Subedar-major Basu, replaced him as the club's secretary.{{Cite web |title=Countrywide success – 1920 to 1929 |url=http://www.mohunbaganclub.com/history/history-1920-1929/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220505224747/http://www.mohunbaganclub.com/history/history-1920-1929/ |archive-date=5 May 2022 |access-date=5 May 2022 |website=Mohun Bagan Club |language=en-US}} Mohun Bagan finished fourth in their league debut, while a separate team of the club made to the semi-finals of the Trades Cup and Coochbehar Cup. The next year, Mohun Bagan reached the second position in the league and the following year, narrowly lost the IFA Shield final to [[Middlesex Regiment]].{{Cite web |title=India - List of Calcutta/Kolkata League Champions |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesi/indiacalchamp.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200802035706/http://rsssf.com/tablesi/indiacalchamp.html |archive-date=2 August 2020 |access-date=5 May 2022 |website=[[RSSSF]]}} On 8 August 1921, the club played its first match against [[East Bengal Club|East Bengal]] in the Coochbehar Cup semi-final, which ended in a goalless draw, but Mohun Bagn went on to beat them in the replay by 3–0 and gave rise to the [[Kolkata Derby]]. In 1922, Mohun Bagan played exhibition matches of football and [[cricket]] against a team of [[Indian South Africans|Indians from South Africa]].{{Cite journal |last1=Bolsmann |first1=Chris |last2=Vahed |first2=Goolam |date=2 November 2017 |title='They Are Fine Specimens of the Illustrious Indian Settler': Sporting Contact between India and South Africa, 1914–1955 |url=https://cogentoa.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/03057070.2017.1379689 |url-status=live |journal=Journal of Southern African Studies |volume=43 |issue=6 |pages=1273–1291 |doi=10.1080/03057070.2017.1379689 |issn=0305-7070 |s2cid=148862123 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221003050545/https://cogentoa.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/03057070.2017.1379689?cookieSet=1 |archive-date=3 October 2022 |access-date=5 May 2022|url-access=subscription }} The following year, Mohun Bagan was invited to [[Rovers Cup]] in [[Bombay Presidency|Bombay]],{{Cite web |last=Nirwane |first=Sarwadnya |date=18 January 2022 |title=Rovers Cup — the second oldest Football tournament in India |url=https://thesportslite.com/football/rovers-cup-everything-you-need-to-know-about-the-tournament/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014043956/https://thesportslite.com/football/rovers-cup-everything-you-need-to-know-about-the-tournament/ |archive-date=14 October 2022 |access-date=14 October 2022 |website=thesportslite.com |publisher=The Sports Lite |location=Mumbai}} where they lost to [[Durham Light Infantry]] by 4–1.{{Cite web |title=India - List of Rovers Cup Finals |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesi/indiaroverscuphist.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924164532/http://www.rsssf.com/tablesi/indiaroverscuphist.html |archive-date=24 September 2015 |access-date=5 May 2022 |website=[[RSSSF]]}} After 35 years of long association of Bhupendra Nath Basu with Mohun Bagan came to an end with his demise in 1924, and was succeeded by Sir Rajendranath Mukherjee. The next year, Mohun Bagan became the first civilian Indian team to be invited to the oldest football tournament in Asia, [[Durand Cup]], where they lost to [[Sherwood Foresters]] in the semi-finals.{{Cite web |last1=Nag |first1=Utathya |last2=Peter |first2=Naveen |date=25 August 2021 |title=Durand Cup in focus as India's oldest football tournament seeks revival |url=https://olympics.com/en/featured-news/durand-cup-2021-history-indian-football-teams-legacy-oldest |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210830155410/https://olympics.com/en/featured-news/durand-cup-2021-history-indian-football-teams-legacy-oldest |archive-date=30 August 2021 |access-date=6 May 2022 |website=Olympics}}{{Cite web |date=27 July 2019 |title=Top 10 moments in Durand Cup history |url=https://khelnow.com/football/durand-cup-2019-history/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210226184414/https://khelnow.com/football/durand-cup-2019-history |archive-date=26 February 2021 |access-date=5 May 2022 |website=Khel Now |language=en-US}} That year Mohun Bagan also failed to win the league and finished second. Significantly, Mohun Bagan also celebrated its [[golden jubilee]] the same year, which was marked with celebrations across the city, match organized featuring renowned former players and, medals and jerseys were distributed to the players. From 1933 to 1939 the club won 29 trophies, also out of 23 [[Kolkata Derby|derbies]], was victorious 12 times, including 1 [[Walkover|walkover win]], drew 10 matches and lost only once.{{cite web |title=Remembering Derby |url=https://themohunbaganac.com/remembering-derbies/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210628161833/https://themohunbaganac.com/remembering-derbies/ |archive-date=28 June 2021 |access-date=4 July 2021}} In 1941, the secretaryship was given to another famed barrister, B.C. Ghosh replacing Sailen Banerjee, who was elected as the club's vice-president, and the following year [[Insurance policy|insurance policies]] were incepted for the medical aid of the injured players during matches, and a medical board composed of reputed doctors was formed to oversee the medical issues.{{cite web |title=Diamond Jubilee – 1940 to 1949 |url=http://www.mohunbaganclub.com/history/history-1940-1949/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220505210606/http://www.mohunbaganclub.com/history/history-1940-1949/ |archive-date=5 May 2022 |access-date=6 May 2022 |website=Mohun Bagan Club}} A [[Trustee|trust board]] was also formed on the initiative of a [[solicitor]] B.K.Ghosh and a barrister Dr. S.K.Gupta for the monetary support of the club. In 1943 and 1944, Mohun Bagan won CFL in succession. In 1944, Secretary Ghosh became the club's vice-president, and Dr. Gupta took charge of the general secretary's office. Meanwhile, a junior football team was formed under the guidance of a former Mohun Bagan player, [[Balaidas Chatterjee|Balaidas Chattopadhyay]], and also efforts were taken to introduce sports like [[Rugby union|rugby]] and [[baseball]] among the youth. In 1945, [[George Curtis (footballer, born 1919)|George Curtis]], who was an [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] player stationed in India as a part of [[Royal Air Force]] in the [[World War II]], took charge of too had to leave for London as the team's head coach and trainer, while Gostho Pal filled in for his duties in the club. Anil Dey was called for the national team as well but stayed behind, and Dhanadaranjan 'Bokai' Sen carried out the captain's duties in the absence of Ao.{{cite web |date=31 January 2007 |title=Former Mohan Bagan custodian passes away |url=https://www.mykhel.com/more-sports/former-mohan-bagan-custodian-passes-away-044534.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220506160327/https://www.mykhel.com/more-sports/former-mohan-bagan-custodian-passes-away-044534.html |archive-date=6 May 2022 |access-date=6 May 2022 |website=My Khel}} In the same year, the [[Kingdom of Afghanistan|Afghan monarch]] invited Mohun Bagan on the occasion of their [[Third Anglo-Afghan War|independence]] celebrations but the club could not attend because of its preplanned agenda. That year, Mohun Bagan successfully defended the IFA Shield against [[Bhawanipore FC|Bhawanipore]] in the final. Ao's on-field excellences for the club and country caught the eyes of [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and was offered a one-year contract but was turned down by him to later pursue [[Bachelor of Medicine, Bachelor of Surgery|MBBS]].{{cite web |date=27 October 2016 |title=Doctor, pioneer, footballer, leader - the remarkable story of T Ao |url=https://www.espn.in/football/story/_/id/17899572/doctor-pioneer-footballer-leader-remarkable-story-talimeren-ao |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210902170332/https://www.espn.in/football/story/_/id/17899572/doctor-pioneer-footballer-leader-remarkable-story-talimeren-ao |archive-date=2 September 2021 |access-date=6 May 2022 |publisher=espn.in}} On the club's [[diamond jubilee]], [[List of chief ministers of West Bengal|West Bengal's Chief Minister]] [[Bidhan Chandra Roy|Dr. Bidhan Chandra Roy]] was invited to exhibition matches hosted by the club, that included three friendlies against [[Allsvenskan|Swedish]] club [[Helsingborgs IF|Helsingborg]]. [[Runu Guha Thakurta]], a renowned forward, was acquired by the club that year. In 1950, India had received a direct qualification to the [[1950 FIFA World Cup|FIFA World Cup]], with club captain Manna being leading the team, but [[All India Football Federation]] refused to play. Despite acquiring the services of some of the famed players the club failed to dominate in major tournaments, where they were regularly outshined by the [[Pancha Pandavas|Pancha Pandav]] led East Bengal and [[Syed Abdul Rahim]]'s [[Hyderabad City Police FC|Hyderabad City Police]] team. S Manna, T Aao, Abhay Ghosh, and R Guhathakurta got their call for the national team to play the [[1951 Asian Games|Asian Games]], and Manna led the team to the [[Football at the 1951 Asian Games|gold medal]].{{cite web |title=The Champions – 1950 to 1959 |url=http://www.mohunbaganclub.com/history/history-1950-1959/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220505210604/http://www.mohunbaganclub.com/history/history-1950-1959/ |archive-date=5 May 2022 |access-date=6 May 2022 |website=Mohun Bagan Club}} In [[1952 Summer Olympics]] three Mohun Bagan players including Manna as the captain and [[Mohammad Abdus Sattar]], who joined the club from Mohammedan in 1950, was called for the national team. Mohun Bagan won the CFL in 1951 after a wait of seven years, the IFA Shield in 1952, and its first Durand Cup in 1953 by 4–0 against [[National Defence Academy (India)|National Defence Academy]] team in the presence of [[President of India|President]] [[Rajendra Prasad|Dr. Rajendra Prasad]]. That year [[Samar Banerjee|Samar 'Badru' Banerjee]] joined the team and formed an important attacking duo with Md. Sattar. During Manna's spell as the captain, he was named among the top 10 captains around the world by [[The Football Association]] in 1953, becoming the first Asian to have the honor.{{cite web |date=14 April 2006 |title=India's greatest footballer |url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/magazine/indias-greatest-footballer/article29646644.ece |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220506160328/https://sportstar.thehindu.com/magazine/indias-greatest-footballer/article29646644.ece |archive-date=6 May 2022 |access-date=6 May 2022 |website=Sportstar |publisher=The Hindu}} In 1954 Mohun Bagan became the first club ever to clinch the [[Double (association football)|double crown]] of [[Kolkata|Calcutta]] — CFL and IFA Shield, and beat the [[Austrian Football Bundesliga|Austrian]] club [[Grazer AK]] by 2–1 and beat the visiting [[Afghanistan national football team|Afghanistan]] by 3–0.{{Cite web |title=History by Decade |url=https://themohunbaganac.com/history-by-decade/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200806224102/https://themohunbaganac.com/history-by-decade/ |archive-date=6 August 2020 |access-date=18 December 2020 |website=Mohun Bagan Athletic Club |language=en-US}} The same year [[Chuni Goswami|Subimal 'Chuni' Goswami]] joined the senior team from the club's youth ranks. Mohun Bagan defended the CFL title successfully till 1956 and won the IFA Shield and its first Rovers Cup in 1956.{{cite web |last1=Nirwane |first1=Sarwadnya |date=18 January 2022 |title=Rovers Cup-the second oldest Football tournament in India |url=https://thesportslite.com/football/rovers-cup-everything-you-need-to-know-about-the-tournament/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014043956/https://thesportslite.com/football/rovers-cup-everything-you-need-to-know-about-the-tournament/ |archive-date=14 October 2022 |access-date=6 May 2022 |website=The Sports Lite}} In December 1954, Mohun Bagan lost a match against [[AIK Fotboll|AIK]] featuring [[Kurt Hamrin]], by 3–1 and in March 1955, played against the visiting [[Soviet Union national football team|Soviet Union]] featuring [[Lev Yashin]] and lost by 3–0.{{cite web |title=A.I.K. (Solna, Sweden) tour of Asia 1954 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesa/aik-oostazietour54.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150317125318/http://rsssf.com/tablesa/aik-oostazietour54.html |archive-date=17 March 2015 |access-date=6 May 2022 |website=RSSSF}}{{cite web |title=1955 USSR and India reciprocal tours |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesu/ussr-india-tours55.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150420150040/http://rsssf.com/tablesu/ussr-india-tours55.html |archive-date=20 April 2015 |access-date=6 May 2022 |website=RSSSF}} Mohun Bagan also played against [[Austria national football team|Austria]] in 1955, but lost by 2–0, and the following year Mohun Bagan, as a representative from India, toured [[Liberal democracy period in Indonesia|Indonesia]], [[Colony of Singapore|Singapore]], [[British Hong Kong|Hong Kong]] and [[Federation of Malaya|Malaya]], which was organized solely by the assistant secretary of the club Dhiren Dey. For the [[1956 Summer Olympics]] in [[Melbourne]], Badru captained the national team. While Krishnachandra 'Kesto' Pal was included in the main squad, Chuni, S Chatterjee, and Sushil Guha were selected as reserved players. The following years were mostly unsuccessful as the club failed to win several major trophies, but during this time, Mohun Bagan obtained the services of [[Jarnail Singh (footballer)|Jarnail Singh Dhillon]] from Rajasthan Club and [[Mariappa Kempaiah]]. Under Dhiren Dey, a strict regime was reinstated in the club and under the coaching of Arun Sinha, the archaic [[Formation (association football)#Pyramid (2–3–5)|2–3–5]] formation was replaced by 3-defenders system.{{cite web |last1=Basu |first1=Jaydeep |date=28 August 2020 |title=From Jarnail To Jhingan: Punjab Flavour to Evolution of Defenders in Indian Football |url=https://www.newsclick.in/jarnail-jhingan-punjab-flavour-evolution-defenders-indian-football |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220426090031/https://www.newsclick.in/jarnail-jhingan-punjab-flavour-evolution-defenders-indian-football |archive-date=26 April 2022 |access-date=6 May 2022 |website=News Click}} Sinha was primarily responsible for properly grooming the likes of Chuni and Jarnail. On 27 April 1962, Gostho Pal received the [[Padma Shri]], becoming the first footballer to do so. The club won its tenth CFL title and IFA Shield that year. Chuni was selected to lead the national team in [[1962 Asian Games]] and won the [[Football at the 1962 Asian Games|gold medal]], with Jarnail Singh playing a pivotal part in the campaign. [[Ashok Chatterjee]], a well-built forward, was another vital addition to the team in 1962. In 1963, Mohun Bagan won CFL again and added Durand Cup to their cabinet after a 2–0 victory against [[Hyderabad City Police FC|Andhra Pradesh Police]]. A new club tent was inaugurated this year by the [[Chief of the Army Staff (India)|Chief of Army Staff]] [[Jayanto Nath Chaudhuri]] and the [[List of chief ministers of West Bengal|Chief Minister]] [[Prafulla Chandra Sen]].{{cite web |title=Mohun Bagan inauguration ceremony of the newly built club tent |url=https://www.facebook.com/MohunBaganAthleticClub1889/videos/1275226216556153 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220810203013/https://www.facebook.com/MohunBaganAthleticClub1889/videos/1275226216556153 |archive-date=10 August 2022 |access-date=10 August 2022 |website=Facebook Live}} 1964 saw Mohun Bagan celebrate its [[platinum jubilee]] with a year-long celebration involving numerous sporting events. Yet the team lost the consistency soon and, in 1967 and 1968 Mohun Bagan won just two trophies, the Shield and Rovers Cup, respectively. Chuni retired from football in 1968 after spending his whole career at Mohun Bagan; thus, the golden team slowly came to a conclusion. In 1969 [[Amal Dutta]] joined and introduced the concept of overlapping [[Defender (association football)#Full-back|full-backs]] in [[Formation (association football)#4–2–4|4–2–4]] to Indian football, for which Bhabani Roy was the primary candidate. With the new strategy in place, Mohun Bagan played scintillating football and captured CFL and IFA Shield with a 3–1 victory against [[East Bengal Club|East Bengal]] in the Shield final. Mohun Bagan struggled to assert dominance in the first half of the 1970s and failed to match their arch-rivals regarding team building. Although they won Rovers Cup from 1970 to 1972, they fared poorly in other major tournaments.{{cite web |title=Encounter with Pele – 1970 to 1979 |url=http://www.mohunbaganclub.com/history/history-1970-1979/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220505210618/http://www.mohunbaganclub.com/history/history-1970-1979/ |archive-date=5 May 2022 |access-date=6 May 2022 |website=Mohun Bagan Club}} With foreign recruits becoming common in East Bengal, Mohun Bagan failed to beat them even once between 1969 and 1974 and lost to their arch-rivals in Durand Cup and IFA Shield finals multiple times. As a result, a host of new players were recruited in 1984, and the most notable names being [[Prasanta Banerjee]], [[Babu Mani]] and Tanumoy Basu, and that led to major successes, including Durand Cup and the Calcutta League title. Later, [[Sisir Ghosh]] was brought in and he made a successful attacking duo with Mani. In 1986 players like [[Satyajit Chatterjee]], [[Aloke Mukherjee]] and Amit Bhadra were to the squad, and the year ended with the Calcutta League, third consecutive Durand Cup and the Federation Cup after a four-year wait and also qualifying for the [[1987 Asian Club Championship]]. Mohun Bagan won twice in the group stage of Asian Championship with 12 goals, half of which were scored by Sisir. However, finishing second in the group failed to progress to the semi-final group. They qualified for ACC once again for the [[1988–89 Asian Club Championship|1988–89 season]] by winning the 1987 Federation Cup and displayed outstanding performance in the group stage, including a 6–0 defeat of [[PFF National Challenge Cup|Pakistani]] team [[Crescent Textile Mills FC|Crescent Textile Mills]] with a hat-trick from Sisir. Still, in the semi-final group, they lost every game and finished at the bottom. At the domestic level, the club failed to win any major tournament except Rovers Cup. Mohun Bagan celebrated their 100th anniversary in 1989 with a grand torch rally starting from [[Basu Bati]] in [[North Kolkata]] and covered several important places in Mohun Bagan's history before reaching the [[Mohun Bagan Ground]]. The [[List of prime ministers of India|Prime Minister of India]] [[Rajiv Gandhi]] arrived for the celebrations and during his speech, he referred to Mohun Bagan as ''"The National Club of India"''.{{cite web |author=Rauf |first=Zohaib |date=2 April 2016 |title=The Inspirational Story of India's First Football Club |url=https://thelogicalindian.com/the-inspirational-story-of-indias-first-football-club/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220325053423/https://thelogicalindian.com/amp/rewind/the-inspirational-story-of-indias-first-football-club/ |archive-date=25 March 2022 |access-date=17 December 2020 |publisher=The Logical India}} Mohun Bagan became the first club to be honored by a postage stamp from the [[Government of India]] on this historical year.{{cite web |author=Ainy |date=24 November 2017 |title=Mohun Bagan Athletic Club |url=https://www.istampgallery.com/mohun-bagan/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200808085009/https://www.istampgallery.com/mohun-bagan/ |archive-date=8 August 2020 |access-date=14 July 2020 |publisher=iStampGallery.com}} === Commercialisation and incoming of foreigners (1990–2000) === The centenary celebrations continued till 1990 when Mohun Bagan played against an assembled team that featured [[Cameroon national football team|Cameroonian]] World Cupper [[Roger Milla]].{{cite web |title=Jyoti Basu: A die-hard Mohun Bagan supporter |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/top-stories/jyoti-basu-a-die-hard-mohun-bagan-supporter/articleshow/5456354.cms |access-date=4 May 2024 |website=[[The Times of India]]|date=17 January 2010 }} The club invested significantly to bring back Krishanu Dey and Babu Mani and along with other major signings like [[Bikash Panji]] and especially [[I. M. Vijayan]], who was being approached by every major club in the country.{{cite web |title=Squad: 1991 – 2000 |url=http://www.mohunbaganclub.com/squad-1991-2000/#google_vignette |access-date=16 May 2024}} In 1991 Mohun Bagan made their first-ever foreign recruitment, which was a Nigerian striker [[Chima Okorie]] from East Bengal, and later the second foreign signing was another Nigerian striker Bernard Operanozie, who would play as a defender.{{cite web |title=Mohun Bagan Squad over the years |date=January 2024 |url=https://www.mbft.in/2024/01/Mohun-Bagan-Squad-Over-The-Years.html |access-date=16 May 2024}} With the arrival of [[Syed Nayeemuddin]] on the bench, Mohun Bagan defended their Rovers Cup and won another Federation Cup in 1992. The following year Oparanozie got the captain's responsibilities after Bhadra got out with injury, and being the club's first foreign captain, he led the team to win Federation Cup again.{{cite web |title=Door Opens for Foreigners – 1990 to 1999 |url=http://www.mohunbaganclub.com/history/656-2/#:~:text=In%201993%2C%20Club%20became%20the,and%20Sikkim%20Governor's%20Gold%20Cup%20. |access-date=16 May 2024}} Mohun Bagan also famously won over [[Croatian First Football League|Croatian]] club [[NK Varaždin (1931–2015)|Varteks]] that year in the group stage of [[DCM Trophy]].{{cite web |title=India - DCM trophy 1993 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesi/indiadcm.html#1993 |access-date=16 May 2024}} 1994 was a decorative year with four trophies including Federation Cup for the third consecutive time, Durand Cup after an eight-year wait, and the CFL.{{cite web |title=Indian Football Moments: Jo Paul Ancheri instant impact at Mohun Bagan |url=https://www.goal.com/en-in/news/india-football-mohun-bagan-jo-paul-ancheri/7mitp7wzcq5e1f2ioyhp26odn |access-date=16 May 2024}} While in [[1993–94 Asian Club Championship]], Mohun Bagan easily thumped [[Club Valencia (Maldives)|Club Valencia]] and [[Ratnam SC|Ratnam]] in the preliminary stage, but after a 4–0 away loss to [[Thai Farmers Bank F.C.|Thai Farmers' Bank]] in the 1st leg of the second round, Mohun Bagan was ejected out of the tournament for refusing to play the 2nd leg in [[Malaysia]]. India was amid [[1994 plague in India|plague outbreak]] and Mohun Bagan failed to win any major trophy for the following two years.{{cite web |title=Spreading their wings in Asia: Some memorable nights of the Green and Maroons |url=https://www.the-aiff.com/article/spreading-their-wings-in-asia-some-memorable-nights-of-the-green-and-maroons |access-date=4 May 2024}}{{football squad on pitch|align=left|GK=[[Hemanta Dora|Hemanta]]|RB=Lorendra|CB=Aloke ([[Captain (association football)|C]])|LB=Reazul|DM=[[Debjit Ghosh|Debjit]]|RCM=[[Satyajit Chatterjee|Satyajit]]|LCM=Basudeb|AM=Amit|CF=[[Chima Okorie|Chima]]|RW=[[Dipendu Biswas|Dipendu]]|LW=Abdul|caption=Mohun Bagan's preferred line-up under Amal Dutta in his "Diamond System".}}In December 1996 the [[National Football League (India)|National Football League]] began as the top-tier league in the country and Mohun Bagan finished at the bottom in the group stage with just one win and was relegated in the next season, which was later revoked by the organizers.{{cite web |title=India Season 1996/97 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesi/india97.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090611104712/http://www.rsssf.com/tablesi/india97.html#nfl1 |archive-date=11 June 2009 |access-date=17 December 2020 |website=[[RSSSF]]}} The club appointed their former coach, Amal Dutta and under him, Mohun Bagan began to play in an innovative [[Formation (association football)#3–4–3|3–4–3]] "Diamond System", which was bolstered by the likes of Abdul Khaliq and Okerie in the front, Mohun Bagan played very offensively, which was rare in Indian football.{{cite web |title=Diamond Touch |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/kolkata/diamond-touch/articleshow/53346818.cms |access-date=4 May 2024 |website=[[The Times of India]]|date=23 July 2016 }} The glamorous success achieved by Amal Dutta and P.K. Banerjee, who was now coaching East Bengal, had given birth to a significant coaching rivalry between them during the 80s, which reached its peak at the [[1997 Indian Federation Cup|1997 Federation Cup]] semi-final. It was one of the most anticipated matches in Indian football history, pitting two fierce rivalries – Mohun Bagan and Amal Dutta against East Bengal and P.K. Banerjee – at one stage. With a record 131,000 attendance at Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan, Mohun Bagan's defensive frailties were exposed by [[Bhaichung Bhutia]], who scored a hattrick in a 4–1 victory for East Bengal.{{cite web |title=Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan (VYBK), Kolkata |url=https://inside.fifa.com/tournaments/mens/u17worldcup/india2017/news/vivekananda-yuba-bharati-krirangan-vybk-kolkata-2847648 |access-date=4 May 2024}} Despite the loss, fans lauded Mohun Bagan's impressive style of play under Dutta's Diamond System. Regardless, the club steered back to win the [[1997–98 National Football League (India)|1997–98 National Football League]] with ten matches unbeaten run and only two losses in the league, under the mentorship of [[T. K. Chathunni]] after Dutta left midway due to internal strife with the club officials. Players like Okorie, [[Dipendu Biswas]], Reazul Mustafa and [[Sri Lanka]]n winger Roshan Pereira played pivotal roles in the team.{{cite web |title=List of Winners/Runners-Up of the National Football League |url=http://www.indianfootball.de/data/nfl.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201027034504/http://www.indianfootball.de/data/nfl.html |archive-date=27 October 2020 |access-date=17 December 2020 |website=www.indianfootball.de}}{{cite web |title=rediff.com: National Football League |url=https://www.rediff.com/sports/nflroll.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303220719/http://www.rediff.com/sports/nflroll.htm |archive-date=3 March 2016 |access-date=17 December 2020 |website=www.rediff.com}} In 1998, [[United Spirits]], a subsidiary of [[Vijay Mallya]] owned [[United Breweries Group]], entered into a partnership with Mohun Bagan by buying a 50% stake in the club's football division and formed a [[joint-venture]] entity named ''United Mohun Bagan Private Limited''.{{cite news |last=Basu |first=Manish |date=25 February 2015 |title=USL moves Sebi on Mohun Bagan sponsorship |url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/HEDxdyOlqAIuu7DnOBuxOP/USL-moves-Sebi-on-renewing-Mohun-Bagan-sponsorship.html%3ffacet=amp |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220325021954/https://www.livemint.com/companies/hedxdyolqaiuu7dnobuxop/usl-moves-sebi-on-renewing-mohun-bagan-sponsorship.html?facet=amp |archive-date=25 March 2022 |access-date=18 December 2020 |work=Mint}} For the first time the club was transformed into a [[Corporation|corporate]] establishment from a [[society]] status, and the name of the club's football division was thus changed to ''McDowell's Mohun Bagan FC''.{{cite web |date=12 August 2015 |title=McDowell's Mohun Bagan |url=https://staticg.sportskeeda.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/mohun-1439386427-800.jpg |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220325021832/https://staticg.sportskeeda.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/08/mohun-1439386427-800.jpg |archive-date=25 March 2022 |access-date=18 December 2020 |website=Sportskeeda}} That season saw them defeat [[Uzbekistan Super League|Uzbek]] giant [[Pakhtakor Tashkent FK|Pakhtakor Tashkent]] in the IFA Shield group stage, and eventually win the Shield. Mohun Bagan signed a host of foreigners for the [[1999–2000 National Football League (India)|1999–00 National Football League]]. Renowned internationals like [[Uzbekistan national football team|Uzbek]] striker [[Igor Shkvyrin]], [[Nigeria national football team|Nigerian]] forward Stephen Abarowei, [[Thailand national football team|Thai]] full-back [[Dusit Chalermsan]] and [[Kenya national football team|Kenyan]] defender [[Sammy Omollo|Samuel "Pamzo" Omollo]], and [[Brazil]]ian [[José Barreto (Brazilian footballer)|José Ramirez Barreto]] joined the club. The Indian contingent in the club was kept almost intact from the last season with the addition of the striker R.C. Prakash and full-back [[Dulal Biswas]], Mohun Bagan comfortably won the league along with Durand Cup and Rovers Cup with former club player Subrata Bhattacharya at the helm. But at the continental stage, got eliminated with an 8–0 defeat against [[Júbilo Iwata]] in the second round of the [[1999–2000 Asian Club Championship|1999–00 Asian Club Championship]].{{cite web|url=https://www.telegraphindia.com/sports/bagan-suffer-humiliation/cid/1221975|title=BAGAN SUFFER HUMILIATION}}{{cite web|url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesa/ascup00.html|title=Asian Club Competitions 1999/2000}} === Heightened foreign influence (2000–2010) === In the [[2001–02 National Football League (India)|2001–02]] season Mohun Bagan's bid to win back-to-back league titles was shattered when they finished second by just a point behind East Bengal. However, Barreto finished as the league's top scorer. Mohun Bagan captured the [[2001 Indian Federation Cup|2001 Federation Cup]] due to the heroics of goalkeeper Bibhas Ghosh and Barreto, who was awarded the tournament's best player.{{cite web |title=Mohun Bagan lift Federation Cup |url=https://www.tribuneindia.com/2001/20010831/sports.htm#12 |access-date=5 May 2024}} Mohun Bagan also triumphed in the Bordoloi Trophy after thrashing [[Thai League 2|Thai]] club [[Rajpracha F.C.|Rajpracha]] 4–0 in the final.{{cite web |title=50th Bordoloi Trophy 2001 [Sep 29-Oct 19, Guwahati, Assam] |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesi/india02.html#bordoloi |access-date=5 May 2024}} Mohun Bagan's squad was joined by another Nigerian, Abdulatif Seriki replacing Omollo. On the final matchday, in a must-win situation against the title contender – [[Churchill Brothers FC Goa|Churchill Brothers]], Mohun Bagan clinched their third league title with a 73rd-minute header by the Nigerian defender Abdul Wastu Saliu assisted by Basudeb Mandal's corner kick. Under Subrata Bhattacharya, Mohun Bagan became the first club to win Federation Cup and NFL in a season. [[Bhaichung Bhutia]], who had joined the club in 2002 missed out on most of the season to injuries producing a negligible impact on the team.{{cite news |title=Mohun Bagan History 2000–2004 |url=http://www.mohunbaganclub.com/History-2000-2004.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100119180022/http://www.mohunbaganclub.com/History-2000-2004.html |archive-date=19 January 2010 |access-date=22 June 2009 |publisher=Mohun Bagan Club}} As a result, Mohun Bagan's on-field form slumped remarkably with the club winning just one major trophy in the form of the IFA Shield in these two years. To make matters worse, in 2004 Mohun Bagan's most influential foreigner – Barreto also left the club and Mohun Bagan finished 7th and 9th in [[2002–03 National Football League (India)|2002–03]] and [[2003–04 National Football League (India)|2003–04]] seasons respectively. The barren period of major trophies also continued next season, as they finished 8th in the league and runner-up in Federation Cup. In 2004, Mohun Bagan became the first Indian club to launch a [[credit card]] in association with [[ICICI Bank]].{{cite web |title=ICICI Bank Ltd. |url=https://www.moneycontrol.com/company-facts/icicibank/history/ici02 |access-date=15 May 2024 |last1=Com |first1=Moneycontrol }} [[File:Salt_Lake_Stadium_(_Yuba_Bharati_Krirangan_)_Kolkata_India_-_FC_Bayern_Munich_Mohun_Bagan_Oliver_Kahn_1.jpg|right|thumb|200px|Crowd at the exhibition match against [[Bayern Munich]].]] With internal problems slowly subsiding, Mohun Bagan assembled a strong side in 2006 that included Barreto and Bhaichung's return, along with a combative Brazilian midfielder [[Douglas Silva (footballer, born 1974)|Douglas Silva]]. The team was further bolstered with top Indian players like [[Sangram Mukherjee]], [[Deepak Mondal]] as well as youngsters like Lalawmpuia Pachuau, [[Lalkamal Bhowmick]] and [[Sushilkumar Singh Chongtham|Sushil Kumar Singh]]. With the sudden resignation of coach Biswajit Bhattacharya, the Brazilian physio of the team, Robson Mattos was hastily promoted as the team's coach. Bhutia and Sangram's collective heroics led them to their 12th Federation Cup. While the [[2006–07 National Football League (India)|2006–07 league season]] did not go well with as many as three foreign coaches taking part during the campaign in the form of Robson Mattos and former players – Chima Okorie and Bernard Oparanozie. [[List of presidents of FIFA|FIFA president]] [[Sepp Blatter]] came to Kolkata and attended Mohun Bagan's won 2–1 Derby win on 15 April 2007.{{cite web |title=FIFA boss gets warm welcome in Kolkata |url=https://www.rediff.com/sports/2007/apr/14blatter.htm |access-date=16 May 2024}} On Mohun Bagan Day, the club became the first in India to launch an official mascot which was a tiger named ''"Baggu"''. In 2007 Mohun Bagan sealed their first-ever [[Indian Super Cup (1997–2011)|Indian Super Cup]] with a 4–0 victory over the league champions [[Dempo SC|Dempo]], with Bhutia scoring a hattrick. In [[2007–08 I-League|2007–08 season]], where NFL got rebranded as [[I-League]], Brazilian coach [[Carlos Roberto Pereira]] took the reins of the team but failed to win any significant accolade. The following season, Mohun Bagan appointed [[Morocco|Moroccan]] coach [[Karim Bencherifa]], who led the team to a record 10-match winning run in the league and a Federation Cup victory. Still, poor performance in his second league resulted in him being sacked midway through the [[2009–10 I-League|2009–10 season]] and putting Satyajit Chatterjee as the interim coach. The only highlight of his second campaign was the 5–3 Derby victory on 25 October 2009.{{cite web |title=Mohun Bagan beat East Bengal 5-3 |date=26 October 2009 |url=https://www.mid-day.com/sports/other-sports/article/mohun-bagan-beat-east-bengal-5-3-61472 |access-date=4 May 2024}} In 2008, Mohun Bagan players got the opportunity to play against [[Germany national football team|German]] icon [[Oliver Kahn]] in his official [[testimonial match]] for [[Bayern Munich]], which also featured Brazilian star [[Zé Roberto]]. The match was played on 27 May 2008 at Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan and finished with Bayern Munich comfortably winning by 3–0.{{cite web |title=Modern great Kahn bids adieu in Kolkata |url=https://fcbayern.com/en/news/2008/05/modern-great-kahn-bids-adieu-in-kolkata |access-date=4 May 2024}} The same year [[Argentina national football team|Argentine]] World Cup winner [[Diego Maradona]] paid a visit to the club tent during a tour to India.{{cite web |title=Diego Maradona and Kolkata: A love story for ages |url=https://www.wionews.com/sports/diego-maradona-and-kolkata-a-love-story-for-ages-345611 |access-date=5 May 2024}} === Struggles in the new decade followed by significant success (2010–2020) === [[File:Bengaluru_FC_vs_Mohun_Bagan.jpg|left|thumb|Bengaluru vs Mohun Bagan, the final match of 2014–15 I-League.]] Mohun Bagan emerged as third ranked Indian team and 611th position worldwide, in the international rankings of clubs during the first ten years of the 21st century (2001–2010) issued by the [[International Federation of Football History & Statistics]] in 2011.{{cite web |date=2010 |title=IFFHS History: The World's Best Club of the First Decade (2001–2010) |url=https://iffhs.de/iffhs-history-the-best-world-club-of-the-first-decade-2001-2010/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328212957/https://iffhs.de/iffhs-history-the-best-world-club-of-the-first-decade-2001-2010/ |archive-date=28 March 2019 |access-date=26 November 2017 |website=iffhs.de |publisher=International Federation of Football History & Statistics |location=Bonn, Germany}} The club though struggled for supremacy in the first five years of the new decade, and the seasons were marked by poor team recruitment, which lacked balance and overpaying for players. The management focused only on recruiting big names while ignoring essential areas of the team which needed bolstering. Some of the foreign stars recruited during this period were [[Odafa Onyeka Okolie]] from Churchill Brothers, with a record salary of {{INR}}1.4 crores per year in 2011, [[Muritala Ali]] from [[Mahindra United FC|Mahindra United]] and [[Tolgay Özbey]] from East Bengal.{{cite web |title=Mohun Bagan sign Odafe for record Rs.2 crore one-year deal |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/top-stories/Mohun-Bagan-sign-Odafe-for-record-Rs-2-crore-one-year-deal/articleshow/8682670.cms |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140115033007/http://articles.timesofindia.indiatimes.com/2011-06-01/top-stories/29607824_1_odafe-onyeka-okolie-mohun-bagan-mohammedan-sporting |archive-date=15 January 2014 |access-date=8 May 2022 |website=The Times of India}} These players failed to replicate their form shown at their former clubs and as a result Mohun Bagan teams which were often built around them also suffered. After an illustrious career at Mohun Bagan, Barreto finally made his exit in 2012. A crowd of over 50,000 turned up at Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan on 6 May 2012 as Barreto played his last match for the club against [[Pune FC|Pune]], where he scored his final goal for the team.{{cite web |date=6 May 2012 |title=Fans brave the heat to bid farewell to Barreto |url=http://zeenews.india.com/sports/football/fans-brave-heat-to-bid-farewell-to-barreto_741926.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140519063701/http://zeenews.india.com/sports/football/fans-brave-heat-to-bid-farewell-to-barreto_741926.html |archive-date=19 May 2014 |access-date=8 May 2022}} The Brazilian ended his career at the club as the first foreigner to score over 200 goals in India for a club with his final tally reading 228 goals in 371 matches.{{cite web |date=14 May 2004 |title=Leading Goal Scorers |url=http://www.rediff.com/sports/nflsco04.htm |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20040828213707/http://www.rediff.com/sports/nflsco04.htm |archive-date=28 August 2004 |access-date=24 October 2018 |work=Rediff.com}} The club endured a phase of five years without a major trophy between 2010 and 2015, the longest such phase since the nation's independence. Although Mohun Bagan won the 2012 [[All Airlines Gold Cup|Airlines Cup]], it wasn't a major trophy anymore. On 29 December 2012, Mohun Bagan was barred from competing in I-League for two years following a decision taken by the league's core committee. The suspension came because Mohun Bagan had refused to take the field in the second half of the match against [[East Bengal F.C.|East Bengal]] on 9 December 2012 due to crowd violence and an unsuitable atmosphere for the continuation of the match.{{cite web |title=Mohun Bagan, East Bengal fans clash, 40 hurt |url=http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/mohun-bagan-east-bengal-fans-clash-40-hurt/1042803/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221003050548/http://archive.indianexpress.com/news/mohun-bagan-east-bengal-fans-clash-40-hurt/1042803/ |archive-date=3 October 2022 |access-date=10 December 2012}} All their results in the [[2012-13 I-League|2012-13 season]] were declared null and void and all their remaining fixtures were cancelled.{{cite news |last1=Roy |first1=Rajat |date=29 December 2012 |title=Century old Mohun Bagan banned from I-League |url=http://www.business-standard.com/india/news/century-old-mohun-bagan-bannedi-league/200951/on |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130102132425/http://www.business-standard.com/india/news/century-old-mohun-bagan-bannedi-league/200951/on |archive-date=2 January 2013 |access-date=29 December 2012 |newspaper=Business Standard India}} However, on 15 January 2013, Mohun Bagan appealed against the decision and were reinstated, but a hefty amount was fined, their officials were suspended from all the AIFF meetings for a year and, the team would start with 0 points and would play out only the remaining 16 fixtures in the league. This did not affect their win-loss and goal difference record in the table.{{cite web |title=AIFF revoke two-year ban on Mohun Bagan |url=http://www.goal.com/en-india/news/1064/i-league/2013/01/15/3673299/aiff-revoke-two-year-ban-on-mohun-bagan |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180630190243/http://www.goal.com/en-india/news/1064/i-league/2013/01/15/3673299/aiff-revoke-two-year-ban-on-mohun-bagan |archive-date=30 June 2018 |access-date=16 January 2013}} This led the team in a dire relegation fight but were successful to avoided it. In the following season, the team performed disastrously and finished 8th in the table, scarcely avoiding relegation. A constant incoming and outgoing of coaches saw established names like Subrata Bhattacharya, [[Subhash Bhowmick]] and Karim Bencherifa, along with younger coaches like [[Stanley Rozario]] and [[Santosh Kashyap]] failing to end the precarious state of the team. Mohun Bagan started the 2014–15 season with Subhash Bhowmick on the bench. However, after finishing as runners in CFL and Bhowmick's lack of mandatory AFC Pro license saw [[Sanjoy Sen]] taking over the reins before Federation Cup. Mohun Bagan's Cup campaign did not go well as they crashed out of the tournament after a 4–1 loss against [[Salgaocar FC|Salgaocar]]. With the likes of [[Katsumi Yusa]], [[Sony Nordé]] and [[Balwant Singh (footballer)|Balwant Singh]] often making the headlines, Mohun Bagan made into the final league match away against the title contender [[Bengaluru FC|Bengaluru]] with just a point advantage, that ended in a draw, thereby winning their first major trophy in five seasons and the first league title in eleven years. Mohun Bagan had reached their [[Anniversary|quasquicentennial]] year of existence in 2014, therefore club organized a huge rally in North Kolkata chiefly to celebrate the anniversary on 1 June 2015.{{cite web |title=Mohun Bagan kicks off quasquicentennial celebrations |url=https://www.thehindu.com/news/cities/kolkata/mohun-bagan-kicks-off-quasquicentennial-celebrations/article6263354.ece |access-date=25 May 2024 |website=[[The Hindu]]}} The celebration was capped off with their league victory achieved the previous month. [[File:Kolkata_Derby.jpg|alt=The Kolkata Derby|left|thumb|Mohun Bagan's 2–1 Kolkata Derby victory, held on 19 January 2020.]] After a breakaway from United Breweries in 2015, Mohun Bagan was once again re-established as a society. Vicuña brought a brand of football to India, which was very similar to that commonly seen in [[Spain]]. The boat perhaps signifies the club's place of establishment; northern [[Kolkata]], on the banks of the [[Ganges]]. The city was the capital during the later 19th century and a prime trade center of [[British Raj|British India]], and the primary mode of transportation was through the waterways. The initial crest of the club varied much due to the lack of any requirement for logo registration, hence any club could use any logo during any tournament. Initially the club crest consisted of the picture of a [[Royal Bengal tiger]] laying either amidst a dense jungle, probably indicating the famous [[Sundarbans]], or simply a [[Arecaceae|palm tree]].{{cite web|url=http://www.sportskeeda.com/football/manchester-united-mohun-bagan-sailing-on-the-same-boat|title=Manchester United and Mohun Bagan sailing the same boat|access-date=24 March 2016|website=sportskeeda.com|date=11 April 2014 |archive-date=8 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160408013132/http://www.sportskeeda.com/football/manchester-united-mohun-bagan-sailing-on-the-same-boat|url-status=live}} The crest with the tiger lying under a palm tree was used during the famous 1911 IFA Shield. A similar logo was used by another [[Maidan (Kolkata)|Maidan]] based club Rajasthan Club, which incited confusions among the locals, henceforth, in 1920s the club came up with a new logo with the iconic sailing boat.{{cite web |title=Club Logo Evolution |url=https://twitter.com/MBArchive1889/status/1675900430986117121?ref_src=twsrc%5Egoogle%7Ctwcamp%5Eserp%7Ctwgr%5Etweet |website=Twitter |publisher=Mohun Bagan Archive |access-date=3 July 2023}} The club's crest is used for all sporting activities other than the football division of the club. The crest for the football division of the club has changed ''[[mutatis mutandis]]'' from time to time due to ownership changes, all the while retaining the signature Green and Maroon colours and the sailboat. After the 2020 rebranding to ATK Mohun Bagan, for the first time the football team crest did not mention the foundation year – ''1889'', which fueled the ongoing controversy over the ownership deal.{{cite web |date=10 July 2020 |title=All you need to know about ATK-Mohun Bagan merger |url=https://www.goal.com/en-in/news/atk-mohun-bagan-jersey-logo-merger-isl-indian-football/nzbkggr93x8a135whx1tklux9 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200710131646/https://www.goal.com/en-in/news/atk-mohun-bagan-jersey-logo-merger-isl-indian-football/nzbkggr93x8a135whx1tklux9 |archive-date=10 July 2020 |access-date=11 July 2020 |website=goal.com}} Later, in 2023, when the football team undergo another rebrand, the new crest incorporated ''1889''.{{cite web |last1=Madhavan |first1=Rahul |date=3 July 2023 |title="1889 is just that icing on the cake" - Mohun Bagan Super Giant fans express delight as the club unveil new logo |url=https://www.sportskeeda.com/indian-football/news-1889-just-icing-cake-mohun-bagan-super-giant-fans-express-delight-club-unveil-new-logo |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230704050217/https://www.sportskeeda.com/indian-football/news-1889-just-icing-cake-mohun-bagan-super-giant-fans-express-delight-club-unveil-new-logo |archive-date=4 July 2023 |access-date=3 July 2023 |website=Sportskeeda}} Priyanath Mitra, the successor of one of the founding families' head Kirti Mitra, had the club's first [[Shades of green#Green (HTML/CSS color)|green]]-[[maroon]] jerseys stitched by a renowned European tailoring shop, Messrs. Bayern Munich Mohun Bagan Oliver Kahn 15.jpg|240px|thumb|[[Oliver Kahn]]'s farewell match against Mohun Bagan at the Salt Lake Stadium]] Mohun Bagan plays most of its home matches at [[Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan]], commonly called Salt Lake Stadium, located in the suburb of Kolkata in [[Bidhannagar]].{{cite web |title=ATK Mohun Bagan FC - Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan [[Government of West Bengal]] under Youth Affairs and Sports Department, the VYBK primarily hosts football matches, apart from occasional [[track and field]] events. The stadium was built in 1984, predominately for matches like [[Kolkata Derby]] that featured attendance too huge for the grounds in [[Maidan (Kolkata)|Maidan]] to accommodate. Before its renovation in 2011, it was the largest football stadium in the world, with a capacity of 120,000. Before the construction and opening of [[Rungrado 1st of May Stadium]] in 1989, it was the largest football stadium in the world. It is currently the fourth-largest sports stadium in Asia by capacity. The gigantic stadium features three tiers of concrete galleries with nine entry gates, including a [[Very important person|VIP]] gate and 30 ramps for the spectators to reach the viewing blocks. === Mohun Bagan Ground === {{Main|Mohun Bagan Ground}} [[File:Mohun Bagan Ground and gallery 09.jpg|thumb|Mohun Bagan Ground in 2018]] The Mohun Bagan Ground is a football stadium located in the Maidan region of central Kolkata, just opposite the [[Eden Gardens]].{{cite web|url=http://www.mohunbaganac.com/about|title=Mohun Bagan Athletic Club|website=mohunbaganac.com|access-date=28 April 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151108012139/http://www.mohunbaganac.com/about|archive-date=8 November 2015|url-status=usurped}} The stadium is operated by Mohun Bagan uses it as a training ground, although in [[2017–18 Mohun Bagan A.C. season|2017]] it had been used for a few of their I-League matches. The office and club tent is adjacent to the stadium. This ground is mainly used for [[Calcutta Football League]] matches. The stadium has galleries on three sides and a rampart on the fourth side. The north side, a contemporary gallery of the stadium, having bucket seats installed, is for the members.{{cite web|url=http://www.feverpitch.in/news.php?newsid=3026&news=Mohun-Bagan-To-Refurbise-Club-Ground|title=Mohun Bagan refurbise club ground|website=feverpitch.in|access-date=12 May 2016|archive-date=13 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160513090233/http://www.feverpitch.in/news.php?newsid=3026&news=Mohun-Bagan-To-Refurbise-Club-Ground|url-status=usurped}} In 1977 [[Mohun Bagan]] became the first club in [[Maidan (Kolkata)|Maidan]] to have floodlights installed in their stadium. The floodlights operated till the mid-1990s, after which they were renovated and inaugurated on 25 February 2016 with an [[IFA Shield]] match between Mohun Bagan U19s and [[DSK Shivajians F.C.|DSK-Liverpool Academy]].{{cite web|url=http://www.mohunbaganac.com/news-detail/newly-installed-floodlights-inaugurated-at-the-mohun-bagan-ground-5019|url-status=dead|title=Newly installed floodlights inaugurated at the Mohun Bagan ground|website=mohunbaganac.com|access-date=12 May 2016|archive-date=10 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160310142242/http://www.mohunbaganac.com/news-detail/newly-installed-floodlights-inaugurated-at-the-mohun-bagan-ground-5019}} After coming in as the principal investor, KGSPL renovated the stadium in the lines of Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan with [[artificial turf]] and upgraded amenities so that it can be used for practice and home matches in Indian Super League and other big tournaments as and when required. == Supporters == [[File:Banner Unfurl.jpg|left|thumb|One of the biggest banners in Indian football unfurled by Mumbai Pune Mariners at the [[Cooperage Ground]] in 2016]] The fans, known as ''Mariners,'' have the reputation of being very loyal and respectful of the club, whom they often consider to be a mother-like figure in their lives. They have had the distinction of the highest attendance during the club's tenure in [[I-League]].{{cite web|url=https://www.goal.com/en-sg/news/3952/asia/2014/07/04/4934968/i-league-attendance-record-highest-for-mohun-bagan|title=Mohun Bagan attendance record|access-date=4 July 2021|archive-date=9 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210709193126/https://www.goal.com/en-sg/news/3952/asia/2014/07/04/4934968/i-league-attendance-record-highest-for-mohun-bagan|url-status=live}} There are several [[Fan club|fanclubs]] dedicated to the club in different parts of [[West Bengal]] and beyond. Mohun Bagan had the highest average attendance with an average home crowd of 17,068 in the 2013–14 season, as per the [[All India Football Federation|AIFF]] reports.{{cite web|url=https://www.the-aiff.com/news-center-details.htm?id=5769|title=Attendance figures of Airtel I-League 2013–14|work=AIFF|access-date=17 November 2015|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304065506/https://www.the-aiff.com/news-center-details.htm?id=5769|url-status=live}} In the [[2014-15 I-League]] season, their vocal support in away matches in [[Pune]], [[Mumbai]] and [[Bengaluru]] was arguably unseen in Indian football until then. but also bringing them together}} Culturally, the rivalry has a lot of significance to the people of Kolkata. Mohun Bagan represents people existing in the [[West Bengal|western part]] of [[Bengal]] (known as ''[[Ghoti people|Ghotis]]''), while East Bengal is primarily supported by people hailing from the eastern part of pre-independence [[Bengal]] (known as ''[[Bangal]]s''). Mohun Bagan vs East Bengal, termed as the Kolkata Derby, is the biggest derby in India and is also considered one of Asia's most heated rivalries. Matches between the two teams are often sold out. The celebrations of a derby win are traditionally marked with dishes prepared from either ''[[ilish]]'' or [[Macrobrachium rosenbergii|''golda chingri'']], depending on which team wins. The East Bengal supporters celebrate their win with ''ilish'' courses, being associated to the eastern region of Bengal (now [[Bangladesh]]), whereas the Mohun Bagan fans celebrate with courses of ''golda chingri.'' Till 17th February 2026, 408 matches have been played between the two teams out of which Mohun Bagan have won 134 matches and East Bengal have won 144 times{{Cite web|url=https://themohunbaganac.com/remembering-derbies/|title=Remembering derbies|access-date=2 June 2020|archive-date=28 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210628161833/https://themohunbaganac.com/remembering-derbies/|url-status=live}} ''(including all competitive matches and exhibition games)'' and rest of the matches ended in draws.{{cite web|url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/football/kolkata-derby-mohun-bagan-vs-east-bengal-statistics-history-rivalry-wins-losses-draws-all-time-i-league-calcutta-football-league/article29303497.ece|title=Kolkata Derby: Stats add intrigue to the Bagan-EB rivalry|website=sportstar.thehindi.com|date=31 August 2019 |access-date=12 September 2019|archive-date=5 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190905032433/https://sportstar.thehindu.com/football/kolkata-derby-mohun-bagan-vs-east-bengal-statistics-history-rivalry-wins-losses-draws-all-time-i-league-calcutta-football-league/article29303497.ece/amp/|url-status=live}} [[File:First official Kolkata Derby news report.jpg|thumb|left|The first official Kolkata Derby news report]] The first match between the sides was played on 8 August 1921 in the Coochbehar Cup, and the semifinal match ended in a 0–0 draw. Mohun Bagan won the replayed semifinal 3–0. Rabi Ganguly scored the first-ever derby goal in that match, and the other two goals were scored by Poltu Dasgupta and Abhilash Ghosh.{{cite web|url=https://sportstar.thehindu.com/football/the-kolkata-derby-they-met-as-early-as-in-1921/article17221788.ece|title=The Kolkata Derby: They met as early as in 1921!}} The first [[Calcutta Football League|CFL]] match between the sides was played on 28 May 1925 in CFL, where East Bengal FC beat Mohun Bagan 1–0. Mohun Bagan holds the record of scoring the fastest goal in a derby (''24 July 1976, a '''17'''-second goal from Md Akbar of Mohun Bagan''). They have the record of winning two consecutive derbies on two successive days (7 and 8 August 1935) and ''had'' ''the unique distinction of losing only one derby in '''7''' years ('''1933 to 1939'''). During this phase, they won '''29''' trophies. Out of '''23''' derbies they won '''12''', drew 10 and lost only 1 against their arch-rivals. It was a golden period in the history of the club''. A few notable victories include the Darbhanga Shield match on 5 September 1934, when Mohun Bagan won '''4–1''' ([[Amiya Deb]] scored all four goals, the only time a player scored four goals in this derby), and a '''5–3''' win in an [[I-League]] encounter on 25 October 2009 ([[Chidi Edeh]] scored four goals). They have won several derbies scoring four goals against East Bengal FC. Mohun Bagan Super Giant, commonly referred to as Mohun Bagan (Bengali: [moɦɔn baɡan]), is an Indian professional football club based in Kolkata, West Bengal. Founded in 1889, it is one of the oldest football clubs in Asia. The club competes in the Indian Super League, the top tier of the Indian football league system. They are the most successful club in India and one of the most successful in Asia, winning a record cumulative number of 265 trophies. They have won more than 5,000 matches in their football history, which is the highest by an Asian club. The club's first notable victory came against the East Yorkshire Regiment in the 1911 IFA Shield final, when its players played barefooted. This victory made Mohun Bagan the first all-Indian club to win championship over a British club, and was a major moment during India's push for independence. 
The club was founded as Mohun Bagan Sporting Club in 1889, which was later changed to Mohun Bagan Athletic Club and often shortened to just Mohun Bagan. From 1998 to 2015, the club took on the name McDowell Mohun Bagan due to sponsorship reasons. In 2017, Mohun Bagan Football Club (India) Pvt Ltd was created as the legal footballing entity of Mohun Bagan Athletic Club. On 16 January 2020, it was announced that the RPSG Group (KGSPL), the owners of ATK FC, along with former cricketer Sourav Ganguly and businessmen Utsav Parekh, acquired an 80% stake in Mohun Bagan Football Club (India) Pvt Ltd. ATK FC was officially disbanded on 1 July 2020, and Mohun Bagan entered the Indian Super League in the 2020-21 season with the name ATK Mohun Bagan FC. In 2023, after severe protests from the Mohun Bagan supporters all around, KGSPL removed the term ATK and changed the name to Mohun Bagan Super Giant.
Mohun Bagan have won a record 7 Indian League titles — the National Football League 3 times, the I-League 2 times and the Indian Super League Shield 2 times. They are the most successful Indian club in the history of the Federation Cup, having won the championship a record 14 times. The club has also won several other trophies, including the ISL playoffs (also known as the ISL Cup) 2 times, the Durand Cup a record 17 times, the Indian Super Cup 2 times, the IFA Shield 23 times, the Rovers Cup a record 14 times and the Calcutta Football League 30 times. Mohun Bagan have also won the Trades Cup a record 11 times, the Sikkim Gold Cup a record 10 times, the Bordoloi Trophy a record 7 times and the All Airlines Gold Cup a record 8 times. The first trophy won by Mohun Bagan was the Cooch Behar Cup in 1904, which they have won a record 18 times.
In the 2024–25 Indian Super League, Mohun Bagan became the first club to successfully defend the League Shield and 7th Indian League title. Mohun Bagan achieved the league and cup double for the first time. In the same season, Mohun Bagan became the 1st ISL club to cross the 50 seasonal points.

The club annually contests in Asia's oldest and biggest rivalry, the Kolkata Derby against its long-time local rival East Bengal, with the first derby match being played on 8 August 1921. Mohun Bagan was one of the founding members of National Football League in 1996, and has never been relegated from the top-tier league of the country. On 29 July 2019, during its 130th year, the club was inducted into the "Club of Pioneers", a network of the oldest existing football clubs around the world.
